Where standing or admissibility is required by the use case, each required property is explicitly and unambiguously represented before consequential reliance.
RequiredEvidence: Governing State Object; authority reference or explicit NOT_ESTABLISHED authority state; applicable standing representation; applicable admissibility representation; use-case applicability criteria; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if relied-upon authority is absent or silently assumed without an explicit authority reference or NOT_ESTABLISHED state, or if standing or admissibility is required by the use case but is absent, ambiguous or silently inferred.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-STATE-003 and LILP-REQ-STATE-004. One structural-state test covers the shared explicit-representation gap. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Material Evidence Object possesses stable identifier
Objective: Establish that each material Evidence Object relied upon by governance possesses an explicit stable evidence identifier.
Preconditions: A material Evidence Object exists in preserved form and is intended to be relied upon by a governance determination or other consequential governance process.
Stimulus: Inspect the Evidence Object identifier and perform repeated read-only references to the same unchanged preserved Evidence Object within the declared scope.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The Evidence Object contains a non-empty explicit evidence identifier, and repeated references to the same unchanged preserved Evidence Object resolve to the same identifier within the declared scope.
RequiredEvidence: Material Evidence Object; explicit evidence identifier field or equivalent representation; declared scope; repeated read-only inspection or reference records demonstrating identifier stability.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the material Evidence Object lacks an explicit evidence identifier, the identifier is empty or ambiguous, or the same unchanged preserved Evidence Object resolves to inconsistent identifiers within the declared scope without an explicit permitted identity rule.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-EVID-001. Stable Evidence Object identity is tested separately from provenance, admissibility and package re-hashability. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Material evidence class is explicitly represented
Objective: Establish that the evidence class of a material Evidence Object is explicitly represented where different epistemic classes could materially affect the determination.
Preconditions: A material Evidence Object is available for a governance determination and the applicable context permits different epistemic evidence classes whose distinction could materially affect the determination.
Stimulus: Inspect the Evidence Object and the determination context and identify the explicitly represented evidence class relied upon for evidentiary evaluation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where epistemic class is material to the determination, the Evidence Object explicitly and unambiguously represents its evidence class before the evidence is relied upon.
RequiredEvidence: Material Evidence Object; explicit evidence-class field or equivalent representation; applicable epistemic-class vocabulary or classification rule; determination context; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if different epistemic classes could materially affect the determination and the relied-upon Evidence Object has no explicit evidence class, has an ambiguous class, or requires the class to be silently inferred from unrelated context.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-EVID-002. Explicit epistemic evidence-class representation remains distinct from provenance, admissibility and evidence-object identity. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: External evidence payload is bound to integrity identifier
Objective: Establish that where integrity of an external evidence payload is claimed, the payload itself or a verifiable content reference to that payload is explicitly bound to the integrity identifier supporting the claim.
Preconditions: An external evidence payload, or a verifiable reference to that payload, is presented and an integrity claim is made using an identified integrity value or mechanism.
Stimulus: Inspect the external payload or verifiable content reference, the claimed integrity identifier and the representation that binds the payload or reference to that identifier.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The integrity identifier is explicitly and unambiguously bound to the external payload or to a verifiable content reference that resolves to the claimed payload, so the integrity claim is attributable to the identified content rather than to an unbound value.
RequiredEvidence: External evidence payload or verifiable content reference; integrity identifier; binding representation; applicable integrity method or metadata; inspection record demonstrating the payload-or-reference relationship.
FailureOracle: FAIL if integrity is claimed but the integrity identifier is detached from the external payload or its verifiable content reference, the binding is absent or ambiguous, or the identifier cannot be attributed to the payload claimed without unsupported inference.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-EVID-007. Payload-or-reference integrity binding remains distinct from independent package re-hashability. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Detected material change is represented separately from predecessor state
Objective: Establish that a detected material change is represented as a distinct delta or change record rather than by mutating, replacing or conflating the preserved predecessor state.
Preconditions: A valid predecessor state exists, a successor or candidate state contains a detected material change, and the comparison basis is available.
Stimulus: Compare the predecessor and changed state, detect the material change, and inspect the resulting representation of that change and its relationship to the predecessor state.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The detected material change is represented in a distinct Delta Object or equivalent change record that is separately identifiable from the predecessor state, while the predecessor state remains preserved as the predecessor.
RequiredEvidence: Preserved predecessor state; changed successor or candidate state; comparison basis; detected material change; distinct Delta Object or equivalent change record; predecessor and successor references; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a detected material change is represented only by mutating, replacing or silently rewriting the predecessor state, or if the change cannot be distinguished as a separate delta representation from the preserved predecessor.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DELTA-002. Separate delta representation is distinct from detecting and classifying material change. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Delta Object identifies affected governing predicates
Objective: Establish that a Delta Object explicitly identifies the governing predicates affected by a material change where the relationship between the change and those predicates can be established.
Preconditions: A valid predecessor state and changed successor or candidate state exist, a material delta has been established, and available evidence permits one or more affected governing predicates to be identified.
Stimulus: Inspect the established Delta Object, comparison evidence and relevant governing predicates and determine which predicates are affected by the material change.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where the relationship can be established, the Delta Object explicitly and unambiguously identifies the affected governing predicates and preserves that relationship as part of the delta representation.
RequiredEvidence: Predecessor and successor or candidate states; Delta Object; changed fields or conditions; applicable governing predicates; evidence supporting the affected-predicate relationship; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if an affected governing-predicate relationship can be established but the Delta Object omits it, represents it ambiguously, or requires the affected predicates to be silently inferred from unrelated context. FAIL if unsupported affected-predicate relationships are invented as established.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DELTA-004. Affected-predicate identification remains distinct from general delta detection and classification. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Claimed identity continuity is supported by sufficient identity evidence
Objective: Establish that where identity continuity is required or claimed, the claimed link is supported by sufficient identity evidence under the applicable identity method rather than by assertion, naming similarity or unsupported inference.
Preconditions: Two or more governance objects, states or chain positions are presented with a claimed identity-continuity relationship, and the applicable identity method and evidence needed to evaluate that relationship are available.
Stimulus: Inspect the claimed continuity link, the identities of the linked objects or states, the applicable identity method and the identity evidence presented in support of the link.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The continuity claim is accepted only where the available identity evidence is sufficient under the applicable identity method to support the claimed link. The supporting evidence and evaluated link remain identifiable and inspectable.
RequiredEvidence: Objects or states participating in the claimed continuity link; stable identifiers or applicable identity material; declared identity or continuity method; identity evidence supporting the link; continuity evaluation record; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if identity continuity is accepted without sufficient supporting identity evidence, if the claimed link depends only on naming similarity or unsupported inference, or if the evidence supporting the claimed continuity relationship cannot be identified and inspected.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CHAIN-002. Positive identity-evidence sufficiency for a claimed continuity link remains distinct from stable object identity, name-based substitution resistance, and failure handling when identity cannot be established. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Material chain-boundary determination is explicitly recorded
Objective: Establish that where a chain-boundary determination materially affects execution, verification or claim scope, the applicable boundary determination is explicitly recorded rather than left implicit or reconstructed after the affected decision.
Preconditions: A governed examination or decision context contains an identifiable chain boundary whose determination materially affects at least one downstream execution, verification or claim-scope consequence.
Stimulus: Evaluate the applicable chain boundary and inspect the resulting determination record before the materially affected execution, verification or claim-scope state is relied upon.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: An explicit chain-boundary determination is recorded and remains identifiable before the materially affected execution, verification or claim-scope consequence is treated as governed. The record preserves the applicable boundary decision and its relationship to the affected downstream context.
RequiredEvidence: Chain context; boundary inputs; chain-boundary determination record; affected execution, verification or claim-scope context; relationship between the boundary determination and affected context; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a material chain boundary affects execution, verification or claim scope without an explicit recorded boundary determination, if the boundary is left only implicit, or if the required determination is retrospectively reconstructed after the affected downstream state.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CHAIN-005. Explicit chain-boundary recording remains distinct from generic determination/execution separation, changed-determination history, bypass restraint, ambiguous-determination failure handling and successor preservation. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: ALLOW permits bounded progression without bypassing later execution predicates
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of ALLOW: an applicable ALLOW determination permits progression only within its declared governance scope and does not itself constitute permission to skip, satisfy or bypass later mandatory execution predicates.
Preconditions: A valid governing state supports an ALLOW determination for a declared bounded scope, and one or more later execution predicates remain independently applicable before consequential execution.
Stimulus: Produce the ALLOW determination, permit the bounded governed progression it authorises, then evaluate the later execution stage without treating ALLOW as satisfaction of the independently required execution predicates.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: ALLOW permits progression only within the declared scope for which it was determined. No consequential execution is inferred from ALLOW alone. All later mandatory execution predicates remain independently required and must be evaluated before execution may proceed.
RequiredEvidence: ALLOW determination; declared scope; governing-state basis; progression record; later mandatory execution predicates; execution-gate or equivalent evaluation record; execution status.
FailureOracle: FAIL if ALLOW is treated as broader authority than its declared scope, if ALLOW itself is treated as completed or permitted consequential execution, or if any later mandatory execution predicate is skipped, presumed satisfied or bypassed solely because ALLOW exists.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-002. The test isolates the semantic boundary of ALLOW itself: bounded governance progression without conversion into execution authority. It remains distinct from generic determination/execution separation and from the later pre-execution gate tests that evaluate mandatory execution predicates. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Determination is attributable to governing state and relied-upon evidence
Objective: Establish that every governance determination preserves an inspectable attribution to the governing state and material evidence on which that determination relied.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request has an identifiable governing state, material evidence set and sufficient basis to produce a governance determination.
Stimulus: Produce the governance determination and independently inspect its recorded basis, governing-state reference and relied-upon evidence references.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The determination remains explicitly attributable to the governing state under which it was made and to the material evidence actually relied upon. The governing-state and evidence references are identifiable and inspectable without inferring or reconstructing the determination basis from unrelated later state.
RequiredEvidence: Determination record; governing-state object or stable governing-state reference; relied-upon evidence objects or stable evidence references; determination basis; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the determination cannot be attributed to the governing state on which it relied, if relied-upon material evidence cannot be identified, or if the claimed determination basis depends on unsupported inference or substitution.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-001. This test isolates positive determination-basis attribution to governing state and relied-upon evidence. It remains distinct from determination/execution separation, chain-boundary recording and ALLOW semantics. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: Execution gate preserves complete material decision evidence
Objective: Establish that the execution gate produces or causes preservation of sufficient evidence to determine what mandatory predicates were evaluated, what values were observed, what determination resulted, whether execution occurred and what consequence, if any, was established.
Preconditions: A consequential request reaches the execution gate with an identifiable set of applicable mandatory predicates, observable predicate values and a downstream execution and consequence state capable of being recorded or explicitly left unresolved.
Stimulus: Evaluate the execution gate for the consequential request, complete or withhold downstream execution as governed, then inspect the evidence preserved by or through the gate process.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The preserved gate evidence is sufficient to identify the predicates evaluated, their observed values, the resulting determination, execution status and consequence status where applicable. Unexecuted, unavailable or unestablished downstream states remain explicitly distinguishable rather than being omitted or inferred as success.
RequiredEvidence: Applicable predicate set; observed predicate values; gate evaluation record; resulting determination; execution status; consequence status or explicit bounded unresolved state; references linking the evidence to the governed request; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the preserved gate evidence cannot establish any required material element: predicates evaluated, values observed, resulting determination, execution occurrence or consequence status where applicable; or if a missing element is silently inferred or manufactured.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-GATE-006. This test isolates the execution-gate evidence-preservation obligation and does not collapse generic gate evaluation, consequence verification or receipt binding into the same test. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: HOLD preserves non-execution while required governance basis remains unresolved
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of HOLD: where required information, authority, governing state or evidence remains unresolved, the HOLD determination preserves non-execution for the contemplated consequential action.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request reaches determination while at least one required information, authority, governing-state or evidence condition remains unresolved and no separately established basis permits consequential execution.
Stimulus: Produce the applicable governance determination while the required condition remains unresolved, then inspect the determination and downstream execution state without supplying the unresolved requirement.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The determination remains HOLD while the required governance basis remains unresolved, and consequential execution remains withheld. HOLD does not silently convert unresolved information, authority, state or evidence into an established predicate and does not imply DENY where prohibition has not independently been established.
RequiredEvidence: HOLD determination; unresolved information, authority, governing-state or evidence condition; determination basis; execution state showing non-execution; timestamps or applicable state references.
FailureOracle: FAIL if consequential execution proceeds while the HOLD basis remains unresolved, if HOLD is treated as satisfying the unresolved requirement, or if the system silently converts HOLD into another determination without a separately supported governance basis.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-003. The test isolates HOLD semantics: unresolved governance basis preserves non-execution. It remains distinct from generic determination/execution separation, missing or ambiguous determination handling, ALLOW semantics and determination-basis attribution. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: DENY represents established prohibition within declared governance scope
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of DENY: the determination represents an established prohibition applicable within the declared governance scope and remains distinguishable from unresolved uncertainty, HOLD or mere absence of execution permission.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request is evaluated within an identifiable governance scope and sufficient governing state, policy, authority and evidence exist to establish a prohibition applicable to the contemplated action.
Stimulus: Produce the applicable governance determination and independently inspect the prohibition basis, declared scope and downstream execution state.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The determination is DENY only where the applicable prohibition is established within the declared governance scope. The prohibition basis and scope remain identifiable, consequential execution is not authorised, and unresolved or merely absent permission is not silently represented as DENY.
RequiredEvidence: DENY determination; established prohibition basis; governing policy or rule; declared governance scope; material governing-state and evidence references; execution state; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if DENY is produced without an established prohibition, if the prohibition is not applicable within the declared governance scope, or if unresolved uncertainty, HOLD or absence of permission is silently represented as DENY.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-004. The test isolates DENY semantics as established prohibition within declared governance scope. It remains distinct from HOLD, ALLOW, NOT_ESTABLISHED and generic determination/execution separation. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: ESCALATE references separately authorised process without itself granting execution authority
Objective: Establish the normative semantics of ESCALATE: the determination identifies or references a separately authorised process while remaining distinct from execution authority unless the governing policy explicitly establishes such authority.
Preconditions: A consequential governance request has a valid basis for escalation and an identifiable separately authorised escalation process. No execution authority is assumed merely from the existence of the escalation determination.
Stimulus: Produce the ESCALATE determination, inspect the referenced escalation process and its authorisation basis, then inspect whether any consequential execution authority has independently been established.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: ESCALATE identifies or references a separately authorised process. The escalation determination does not itself grant consequential execution authority unless the applicable governing policy explicitly establishes that authority. Escalation routing and execution authority remain independently inspectable.
RequiredEvidence: ESCALATE determination; escalation-process identifier or reference; evidence that the referenced process is separately authorised; applicable governing policy; execution-authority state; execution state; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if ESCALATE does not identify or reference a separately authorised process, or if the escalation determination itself is treated as granting consequential execution authority without explicit governing-policy support.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-005. The test isolates ESCALATE semantics and the separation between escalation routing and execution authority. It remains distinct from ALLOW, HOLD, DENY and generic determination/execution separation. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution or conformance.

Title: INVALID remains distinguishable from NOT_ESTABLISHED
Objective: Establish that INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED remain distinct determination states: an object, proposition or determination that fails an applicable validity criterion is not silently treated as merely unresolved, and an unresolved basis is not silently treated as established invalidity.
Preconditions: Two bounded governance evaluation cases are available under an identifiable governing context: one case has a directly inspectable basis for failing an applicable validity criterion, while the second lacks sufficient established basis for the required proposition but does not independently establish that the proposition or object is invalid.
Stimulus: Evaluate both bounded cases under the applicable governance rules and inspect the resulting determination state, supporting basis and downstream non-execution state without repairing, substituting or supplying missing evidence.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The case with an established validity failure is represented as INVALID when that determination is supported by the applicable governing rule. The unresolved case remains NOT_ESTABLISHED where the required basis cannot be established. INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED remain separately attributable and are not substituted for one another solely because both prevent unsupported consequential progression.
RequiredEvidence: Applicable validity criterion or rule; evidence establishing the validity failure for the INVALID case; unresolved or insufficient basis for the NOT_ESTABLISHED case; resulting determination states; governing-context references; execution state; timestamps or equivalent inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if an unresolved basis is represented as INVALID without an established validity failure, if an established validity failure is silently represented only as NOT_ESTABLISHED, or if the implementation cannot preserve an inspectable distinction between INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001R human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DET-007. The test isolates the required distinction between INVALID and NOT_ESTABLISHED. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Material claim identifies claim class or unambiguously identifies claimed property
Objective: Establish that every material claim identifies its claim class or otherwise makes the specific property being claimed unambiguous, so that the claim cannot silently shift between materially different claim meanings.
Preconditions: A material claim is available with an associated evidence basis, evaluated property and declared context. The claim representation can be inspected independently of undocumented author intent.
Stimulus: Inspect the material claim and determine whether it explicitly identifies its claim class or otherwise represents the claimed property with sufficient specificity to distinguish it from materially different claim properties.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The material claim explicitly identifies its claim class or unambiguously identifies the property being claimed. The claim meaning remains inspectable from the governed claim representation and does not depend on unstated assumptions, surrounding implication or retrospective interpretation to determine what property was asserted.
RequiredEvidence: Material claim; claim-class identifier where used; explicit claimed-property representation where claim class is not used; evaluated property; evidence basis; declared context; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a material claim neither identifies its claim class nor makes the claimed property unambiguous, if materially different claim meanings remain plausible from the governed representation, or if the claimed property can only be established through undocumented or retrospective interpretation.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001S human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-001. The test isolates claim-class or equivalent claimed-property identification. It remains distinct from evidence sufficiency, claim scope, independent-verification prerequisites, profile completeness and conformance-status assignment. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Claim identifies the subject to which it applies
Objective: Establish that a claim identifies the subject to which the claimed property applies, preserving attribution between the assertion and the specific system, object, component, process, profile, evidence package or other declared subject.
Preconditions: A claim exists concerning a bounded subject and claimed property. The subject can be independently identified within the governed context and is distinguishable from other possible subjects.
Stimulus: Inspect the claim representation and determine whether the subject to which the claim applies is explicitly identified or otherwise unambiguously bound to the claim.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The claim identifies or unambiguously binds the subject to which it applies. The claimed property cannot silently transfer to another system, object, component, process, profile, evidence package or other subject merely because that subject appears in the same context.
RequiredEvidence: Claim; subject identifier or unambiguous subject binding; claimed property; declared context; relevant evidence or provenance reference; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the subject of the claim is absent or materially ambiguous, if multiple materially different subjects could reasonably receive the claim, or if the claimed property can be silently attributed to a different subject without a separately established claim.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001S human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-002. The test isolates claim-subject identification and attribution. Claim subject remains distinct from claim class, claimed property, evaluated scope and evidence sufficiency. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Time-sensitive claim identifies its temporal scope
Objective: Establish that where time materially affects the validity of a claim, the claim identifies the temporal scope within which the claimed property is asserted to hold.
Preconditions: A material claim concerns a property whose validity can materially vary with time, state epoch, effective period, observation time or other temporally bounded condition. The supporting evidence and applicable temporal context are inspectable.
Stimulus: Inspect the governed claim representation and determine whether it identifies the applicable temporal scope or otherwise unambiguously binds the claimed property to the relevant time, period, epoch or temporal condition.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where time materially affects validity, the claim identifies or unambiguously preserves its temporal scope. The claim does not silently present a historically valid, future-valid, expired or otherwise time-bounded property as timeless or currently valid outside the supported temporal scope.
RequiredEvidence: Claim; claimed property; temporal-scope identifier or unambiguous temporal binding; relevant timestamps, effective period, state epoch or time-sensitive condition; supporting evidence; applicable status; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if time materially affects claim validity and the claim omits or materially obscures its temporal scope, if a historically or otherwise temporally bounded property is silently represented as timeless or current, or if the applicable temporal scope can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in the governed claim representation.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001T human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-004. The test isolates temporal claim-scope identification where time materially affects validity. It remains distinct from general claim scope and changed-condition reassessment. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Conformance claim identifies exact standard version and profile
Objective: Establish that every conformance claim identifies the exact standard version and conformance profile relied upon, so that the claimed conformance basis is bounded, reproducible and not silently transferred across different standard versions or profiles.
Preconditions: A conformance claim is available. The governing standard has an identifiable version and the applicable conformance profile is identifiable and distinguishable from other versions or profiles.
Stimulus: Inspect the governed conformance claim and determine whether it explicitly identifies the exact standard version and the specific conformance profile on which the claim relies.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The conformance claim explicitly identifies or unambiguously binds both the exact standard version and the conformance profile relied upon. The claim cannot silently inherit, substitute or transfer conformance across a different standard version, profile or unspecified conformance basis.
RequiredEvidence: Conformance claim; exact standard identifier and version; conformance-profile identifier; applicable profile definition; claim scope; supporting requirements-matrix or determination evidence; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a conformance claim omits or materially ambiguates the standard version or conformance profile relied upon, if more than one materially different version or profile could support the wording, or if the claim can be transferred to another version or profile without a separately established conformance basis.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001V human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CLAIM-008. The test isolates exact standard-version and conformance-profile identification in the claim itself. It remains distinct from requirements-matrix completeness within an already declared profile. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: PL3 identifies the procedure and evidence used
Objective: Establish that a PL3 proof-level claim or governed PL3 record identifies both the procedure relied upon and the evidence used to support the claimed result.
Preconditions: A PL3 claim or governed PL3 determination exists; a procedure was relied upon for the bounded evaluated property; and an evidence set was used in reaching the PL3 claim or determination.
Stimulus: Inspect the PL3 claim or governed PL3 record and determine whether the relied-upon procedure and the evidence used are each explicitly identified or otherwise unambiguously bound to the PL3 representation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The PL3 representation identifies or unambiguously binds both the procedure relied upon and the evidence used. Procedure identity and evidence identity remain separately inspectable, and neither is silently inferred from an undocumented process, surrounding context or retrospective reconstruction.
RequiredEvidence: PL3 claim or determination; bounded evaluated property; procedure identifier or unambiguous procedure reference; evidence identifiers or evidence-set reference; applicable result; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if PL3 is positively represented while the procedure used is absent or materially ambiguous, the evidence used is absent or materially ambiguous, either can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in the governed PL3 representation, or the representation cannot distinguish the relied-upon procedure from the supporting evidence.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001W human semantic review of LILP-REQ-PROOF-005. The test isolates PL3 procedure-and-evidence identification. It remains distinct from generic evidence-basis traceability and from withholding a positive claim where the required proof level cannot be established. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: PL5 identifies reproduction conditions and result
Objective: Establish that a PL5 proof-level claim or governed PL5 record identifies both the reproduction conditions under which the evaluated property was reproduced and the result obtained under those conditions.
Preconditions: A PL5 claim or governed PL5 determination exists; a bounded evaluated property has been subjected to reproduction; the relevant reproduction conditions are knowable; and a reproduction result exists.
Stimulus: Inspect the PL5 claim or governed PL5 record and determine whether the reproduction conditions and the resulting outcome are each explicitly identified or otherwise unambiguously bound to the PL5 representation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The PL5 representation identifies or unambiguously binds both the reproduction conditions and the result obtained under those conditions. The conditions and result remain separately inspectable and preserve the bounded circumstances under which reproduction occurred, without silently generalising the result beyond those conditions.
RequiredEvidence: PL5 claim or determination; bounded evaluated property; reproduction-condition identifiers or complete bounded condition description; reproduced result; applicable procedure or method reference where preserved; supporting evidence; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if PL5 is positively represented while the reproduction conditions are absent or materially ambiguous, the result is absent or materially ambiguous, the result cannot be bound to the stated reproduction conditions, the conditions or result can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in the governed PL5 representation, or the reproduced result is silently represented as applying beyond the conditions under which it was obtained.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001X human semantic review of LILP-REQ-PROOF-007. The test isolates PL5 reproduction-condition and result identification. It remains distinct from PL3 procedure-and-evidence identification, generic evidence-basis traceability, and independent-verification prerequisites. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Mandatory NOT_ESTABLISHED blocks profile PASS unless explicitly permitted
Objective: Establish that an applicable mandatory requirement with status NOT_ESTABLISHED prevents a PASS conformance determination unless the governing requirement itself explicitly permits NOT_ESTABLISHED for that requirement in the declared profile and scope.
Preconditions: A conformance determination is being evaluated; at least one mandatory requirement applicable to the declared profile and scope has status NOT_ESTABLISHED; and the governing requirement text is available for inspection of any explicit permission for that state.
Stimulus: Attempt to issue PASS for the affected conformance determination while the applicable mandatory requirement remains NOT_ESTABLISHED, then inspect whether the requirement itself explicitly permits that state.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: PASS is withheld while an applicable mandatory requirement remains NOT_ESTABLISHED unless the requirement itself explicitly permits NOT_ESTABLISHED. Any exception is accepted only when the permission is explicit, requirement-specific, applicable to the declared profile and scope, and traceable to the governing requirement text. Silence, ambiguity or surrounding inference does not constitute permission.
RequiredEvidence: Conformance determination; declared profile and scope; mandatory requirement identifier; governing requirement text and version; applicability determination; NOT_ESTABLISHED status evidence; explicit permission clause where relied upon; requirements-matrix entry; determination basis; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if PASS is issued while an applicable mandatory requirement remains NOT_ESTABLISHED and that requirement does not explicitly permit the state, if silence or ambiguity is treated as permission, or if an exception is inferred from material other than the governing requirement itself without an explicit requirement-specific permission.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001Z human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CONF-007. This test is distinct from mandatory FAIL blocking profile PASS because NOT_ESTABLISHED carries a requirement-specific explicit-permission exception. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: LILP-FULL claim blocked by mandatory FAIL or NOT_ESTABLISHED
Objective: Establish that LILP-FULL is not claimed while any mandatory requirement applicable to the declared profile and scope remains FAIL or NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Preconditions: A LILP-FULL claim is contemplated or presented; the declared profile and scope are identifiable; applicable mandatory requirements have recorded conformance statuses; and at least one applicable mandatory requirement remains FAIL or NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Stimulus: Attempt to make or preserve a LILP-FULL claim while inspecting the statuses of all mandatory requirements applicable to the declared profile and scope.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The LILP-FULL claim is withheld or refused while any applicable mandatory requirement remains FAIL or NOT_ESTABLISHED. The blocking requirement and status remain identifiable in the claim determination basis and evidence history, and the stronger LILP-FULL claim is not inferred from narrower partial, bounded or non-full conformance outcomes.
RequiredEvidence: Attempted LILP-FULL claim; declared profile and scope; complete applicable mandatory-requirement set; requirements matrix; recorded conformance statuses; blocking FAIL or NOT_ESTABLISHED requirement identifiers; determination basis; supporting evidence; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if LILP-FULL is claimed while an applicable mandatory requirement remains FAIL or NOT_ESTABLISHED, if a blocking status is omitted or obscured from the claim basis, or if a narrower conformance outcome is silently represented as LILP-FULL.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 001Z human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CONF-011. This test governs the explicit LILP-FULL claim ceiling across both mandatory FAIL and NOT_ESTABLISHED states and remains distinct from generic profile-PASS and evidence-insufficiency controls. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Conformance determination is traceable to requirements matrix and test evidence
Objective: Establish that a conformance determination preserves traceability to the specific requirements matrix and the test evidence on which that determination relies.
Preconditions: A conformance determination exists or is being prepared; the declared profile and scope are identifiable; the applicable requirements matrix exists; and test evidence relied upon by the determination is available or explicitly referenced.
Stimulus: Inspect the conformance determination and attempt to trace its basis to the governing requirements-matrix entries and the corresponding test evidence supporting the recorded requirement statuses and resulting determination.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The conformance determination identifies or unambiguously binds the applicable requirements matrix and the test evidence supporting the determination. The traceability permits the determination basis to be followed from the claimed profile and scope through applicable requirement entries to the relevant test evidence without retrospective reconstruction, silent substitution or unsupported inference.
RequiredEvidence: Conformance determination; declared profile and scope; exact requirements-matrix identifier and version; applicable requirement identifiers and statuses; test identifiers where applicable; referenced test evidence or evidence-package identifiers; provenance; linkage or binding record; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the conformance determination cannot be traced to its applicable requirements matrix, cannot be traced to the test evidence supporting the determination, relies on ambiguous or substituted evidence, requires retrospective reconstruction of a missing linkage, or presents traceability to only one of the required matrix or test-evidence layers.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002A human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CONF-012. This definition establishes the abstract traceability test only. It does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Reproducibility evidence package identifies material necessary to perform reproduction
Objective: Establish that where reproducibility is claimed, the evidence package contains or identifies the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction.
Preconditions: A reproducibility claim exists; the claimed reproduced property and bounded reproduction context are identifiable; an evidence package supports the claim; and the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction is knowable.
Stimulus: Inspect the reproducibility evidence package and attempt to locate, from the package itself or its explicit references, the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The evidence package contains or unambiguously identifies the material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction. Required material can be resolved from preserved package content or explicit package references without retrospective reconstruction, silent substitution or reliance on undocumented contextual knowledge. This control establishes material preservation or identification and does not by itself establish that an independent reproduction has succeeded.
RequiredEvidence: Reproducibility claim; evidence package identifier and version; bounded reproduced property; reproduction-material inventory or explicit material references; applicable procedure or method reference; reproduction conditions where preserved; provenance; package linkage or manifest; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if reproducibility is positively claimed while material necessary to perform the claimed reproduction is absent, materially incomplete, ambiguously referenced, cannot be resolved from the evidence package or its explicit references, or can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved or identified by the governed evidence package.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002B human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CONF-017. This test addresses reproduction-material preservation or identification and remains distinct from T16-015 reproduction-condition and result representation. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, reproduction success, result or conformance.

Title: Claimed profile executes all applicable mandatory general falsification tests
Objective: Establish that every mandatory general falsification test applicable to a claimed conformance profile and its declared scope has been executed before that profile is positively claimed.
Preconditions: A conformance profile and scope are declared; the mandatory general falsification tests applicable to that profile and scope are identifiable; and a positive conformance-profile claim is contemplated or presented.
Stimulus: Enumerate the mandatory general falsification tests applicable to the declared profile and scope, then inspect the execution evidence for each required test before evaluating the claimed profile.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Every mandatory general falsification test applicable to the claimed profile and declared scope has a distinct preserved execution record. A positive profile claim is not supported merely by test definition existence, planned execution, status assignment, inferred coverage or execution of only a subset of the applicable mandatory test set.
RequiredEvidence: Claimed profile and declared scope; governing profile definition; complete applicable mandatory general falsification-test set; test identifiers and definitions; execution records for every applicable mandatory test; execution provenance; associated results or status evidence where applicable; completeness inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a claimed conformance profile is positively represented while one or more applicable mandatory general falsification tests lack preserved execution evidence, if definition existence or planned execution is substituted for actual execution, if only a subset of the required mandatory test set was executed, or if applicability is silently narrowed to avoid a required test.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002B human semantic review of LILP-REQ-TEST-001. This test distinguishes test-definition existence, mapping, status assignment and planned execution from preserved execution of every applicable mandatory general falsification test. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution of this test, result or conformance.

Title: Test evidence preserves input expected result observed result and determination
Objective: Establish that evidence for a test preserves the test input, expected result, observed result and resulting determination as distinct inspectable elements of the test record.
Preconditions: A bounded test instance exists; its test input and expected result are identifiable; the test has produced or recorded an observed result; and a determination has been made or is being recorded.
Stimulus: Inspect the preserved test evidence and attempt to identify and bind the test input, expected result, observed result and determination to the same bounded test instance.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The test evidence explicitly contains or unambiguously binds the test input, expected result, observed result and determination. Expected and observed results remain distinguishable, the determination is traceable to the preserved test instance, and no required element depends on retrospective reconstruction, silent substitution or undocumented contextual knowledge.
RequiredEvidence: Test identifier; test definition or bounded test instance; preserved test input; expected result; observed result; determination; provenance; evidence or receipt identifiers; linkage or binding record; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the test evidence omits or materially ambiguates the test input, expected result, observed result or determination; if expected and observed results cannot be distinguished; if the determination cannot be bound to the same preserved test instance; or if any required element can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in the test evidence.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002C human semantic review of LILP-REQ-TEST-002. This definition preserves the four-part test-evidence tuple of input, expected result, observed result and determination. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, test execution, result or conformance.

Title: Unexecuted mandatory falsification test blocks PASS absent established NOT_APPLICABLE rationale
Objective: Establish that PASS is not issued for a declared conformance profile when a mandatory falsification test required by that profile and scope has not been executed, unless a valid NOT_APPLICABLE rationale for that test is separately established.
Preconditions: A conformance profile and scope are declared; at least one mandatory falsification test required by that profile and scope is identifiable; the required test lacks an execution record; and a PASS conformance determination is contemplated or presented.
Stimulus: Attempt to issue or preserve PASS while the required mandatory falsification test remains unexecuted, then inspect whether a NOT_APPLICABLE rationale specific to that test has been separately established for the declared profile and scope.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: PASS is withheld while a required mandatory falsification test remains unexecuted unless a NOT_APPLICABLE rationale for that specific test is established. Any non-execution exception is accepted only when the rationale is explicit, test-specific, applicable to the declared profile and scope, traceable to the governing applicability basis, and preserved in the determination evidence. Silence, omission, planned execution or inferred inapplicability does not establish NOT_APPLICABLE.
RequiredEvidence: Declared conformance profile and scope; mandatory falsification-test identifier and definition; governing applicability basis; execution-status evidence showing the required test was not executed; any asserted NOT_APPLICABLE status and rationale; rationale provenance; requirements-matrix or equivalent governed status record; conformance determination basis; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if PASS is issued while a mandatory falsification test required by the declared profile and scope remains unexecuted and no valid NOT_APPLICABLE rationale has been established for that test; if omission or silence is treated as NOT_APPLICABLE; if planned or future execution is substituted for completed execution; or if a NOT_APPLICABLE rationale is ambiguous, non-specific, unsupported or outside the declared profile and scope.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002E human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CONF-020. This test governs the exception boundary between required falsification-test execution and separately established NOT_APPLICABLE rationale. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Self-assessed PASS identifies itself as self-assessed when independence could be inferred
Objective: Establish that a self-assessed PASS explicitly identifies its self-assessed status where the claim could otherwise reasonably be understood as independent verification.
Preconditions: A PASS conformance result has been produced by self-assessment; the claim or presentation context is identifiable; and the wording or surrounding presentation could reasonably permit a reader to understand the result as independently verified if the assessment mode were not disclosed.
Stimulus: Inspect the PASS claim, its presentation context and the preserved assessment provenance, then determine whether the claim explicitly identifies itself as self-assessed before or at the point where the conformance result is represented.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where ambiguity with independent verification could reasonably arise, the PASS claim explicitly identifies or unambiguously binds itself as self-assessed. The assessment mode is visible in the governed claim representation and does not depend on hidden metadata, later clarification, absence of an external verifier or undocumented contextual knowledge. The claim does not silently acquire the appearance of independent verification.
RequiredEvidence: PASS claim or governed claim record; declared conformance profile and scope; assessment-mode representation; assessor identity or responsible assessment entity; assessment provenance; public or recipient-facing presentation context where applicable; supporting conformance determination; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a self-assessed PASS is presented without identifying itself as self-assessed where the wording or context could reasonably be understood as independent verification; if self-assessment status is available only through hidden or unrelated metadata; if later clarification is required to correct the apparent assessment status; or if the claim is allowed to imply independent verification without separately established evidence supporting that stronger status.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002F human semantic review of LILP-REQ-WORD-001. This control distinguishes positive self-assessment labelling from controls that merely reject unsupported independent-verification claims. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: NOT_APPLICABLE status identifies scope-specific rationale
Objective: Establish that every NOT_APPLICABLE conformance status includes a rationale establishing why the identified requirement does not apply to the declared conformance scope.
Preconditions: A declared conformance profile and scope exist; a specific requirement has been assigned NOT_APPLICABLE; the requirement and governing applicability basis are identifiable; and the NOT_APPLICABLE status is being used in a conformance determination or governed status record.
Stimulus: Inspect the NOT_APPLICABLE status, its associated requirement, the declared conformance scope and the preserved rationale, then evaluate whether the rationale establishes why that requirement does not apply to that scope.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The NOT_APPLICABLE status includes or unambiguously binds a requirement-specific rationale establishing why the identified requirement does not apply to the declared conformance scope. The rationale is preserved with the governed status, traceable to the requirement and scope relied upon, and sufficiently explicit to distinguish established inapplicability from omission, silence, convenience, unsupported assertion or undocumented contextual inference.
RequiredEvidence: Requirement identifier and governing requirement text or version; declared conformance profile and scope; NOT_APPLICABLE status record; requirement-specific inapplicability rationale; governing applicability basis where applicable; rationale provenance; requirements-matrix or equivalent governed status entry; conformance determination basis; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if NOT_APPLICABLE is assigned without a preserved rationale establishing why the requirement does not apply to the declared scope; if the rationale is absent, materially ambiguous, generic, unsupported or not bound to the specific requirement and scope; if omission or silence is treated as inapplicability; or if the rationale can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved with or explicitly referenced by the governed status record.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002G human semantic review of LILP-REQ-CONF-008. This control is generic to NOT_APPLICABLE requirement status and remains distinct from T16-021, which is bounded to the non-execution exception for mandatory falsification tests. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Each additional claimed property has property-specific evidence and bounded verification method
Objective: Establish that where one or more additional properties are claimed beyond the base conformance result, each separately claimed property is supported by its own identifiable evidence basis and bounded verification method.
Preconditions: A governed claim or conformance representation exists; at least one property is claimed in addition to the base conformance result or status; each additional claimed property is identifiable; and the supporting evidence and verification basis presented for the claim can be inspected.
Stimulus: Inspect each additional claimed property separately and determine whether that property is explicitly bound to supporting evidence and to a bounded verification method capable of evaluating the claimed property within its declared scope.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Each additional claimed property identifies or unambiguously binds its own supporting evidence and bounded verification method. The property, evidence basis and verification method remain separately inspectable and traceable to one another. Evidence or method support for one property is not silently transferred to a different property, and a generic conformance PASS, shared evidence set, undocumented procedure or surrounding context does not by itself establish support for an additional property.
RequiredEvidence: Governed claim or conformance representation; identifier or explicit description for each additional claimed property; property-specific supporting evidence or evidence-set reference; bounded verification-method identifier, procedure reference or complete method description for each property; declared scope and applicable conditions; provenance; resulting determination or claim status; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if any additional claimed property lacks identifiable supporting evidence or a bounded verification method; if evidence or method support cannot be bound to the same specific property; if support for one property is silently reused to establish another materially different property without a separately established basis; if a generic PASS or undifferentiated evidence set is treated as sufficient by itself; or if the required property-to-evidence-to-method relationship can only be reconstructed retrospectively from information not preserved in or explicitly referenced by the governed claim record.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002H human semantic review of LILP-REQ-WORD-005. This generic property-specific evidence-and-verification-method control remains distinct from T16-014 and T16-015, which are bounded to PL3 and PL5 representations respectively. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Public conformance claim is accompanied by declared profile
Objective: Establish that a public LILP conformance claim is accompanied at the point of representation by the declared conformance profile to which the claim applies.
Preconditions: A LILP conformance claim is prepared for public presentation or publication; a declared conformance profile exists for the claim; the public-facing claim representation and profile identity are inspectable.
Stimulus: Inspect the public conformance claim at the point where it is presented and determine whether the declared conformance profile accompanies, is displayed with, or is unambiguously bound from that public claim representation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The public conformance claim includes, displays or unambiguously binds the declared conformance profile at the point of representation. The profile identity is available from the governed public claim itself or through an explicit claim-bound reference that a recipient can inspect without relying on hidden metadata, a private internal record, unrelated surrounding material or later clarification. The claim cannot silently appear profile-independent.
RequiredEvidence: Public conformance claim or preserved public-facing representation; declared conformance profile identifier; applicable standard and version where preserved; explicit profile display or claim-bound profile reference; publication or presentation context; linkage between claim and profile; provenance; supporting conformance determination; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a public conformance claim is presented without the declared profile accompanying or being unambiguously bound to the claim; if the applicable profile is available only through hidden metadata, a private internal record, unrelated material or later clarification; if multiple profiles could reasonably apply and the public claim does not identify which one governs; or if the claim can be understood as profile-independent because the profile-to-claim relationship is not preserved at the point of representation.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002I human semantic review of LILP-REQ-WORD-007. This control governs public-claim/profile accompaniment and remains distinct from T16-013 profile identification in a conformance claim and T16-022 self-assessment disclosure. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Material trust boundaries are identified within declared conformance scope
Objective: Establish that the LILP implementation explicitly identifies material trust boundaries relevant to the declared conformance scope so that material transitions between trust domains, trust assumptions or independently governed components are inspectable rather than implicit.
Preconditions: A declared LILP conformance scope exists; the implementation, actors, components, interfaces and material evidence or consequence flows within that scope are inspectable; trust relationships relevant to the declared scope can be evaluated.
Stimulus: Inspect the declared conformance scope and the implementation representation for material trust boundaries, including boundaries between actors, components, systems, interfaces, evidence sources, governance domains or execution surfaces where trust assumptions materially change.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Each material trust boundary relevant to the declared conformance scope is explicitly identified and is inspectably bound to the affected actor, component, interface, flow or governance transition. The representation permits an examiner to distinguish the relevant sides of the boundary and the material trust relationship or assumption without relying solely on undocumented implementation knowledge, hidden context or retrospective explanation.
RequiredEvidence: Declared conformance scope; architecture, inventory, structured record or equivalent representation identifying material trust boundaries; affected actors, components, interfaces, evidence flows or consequence flows; material trust assumptions or transition context; provenance of the boundary representation; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a material trust boundary relevant to the declared conformance scope exists but is omitted, materially ambiguous, not bound to the affected actor, component, interface or flow, identifiable only through undocumented or hidden implementation context, substituted by a boundary outside the declared scope, or reconstructed retrospectively after the examination.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002K human semantic review of LILP-REQ-SEC-001. This control is specific to identification of material trust boundaries relevant to declared conformance scope and remains distinct from evidence provenance, evidence-object identity, integrity and independent re-hashability controls. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Cryptographic signature identifies its verification basis
Objective: Establish that where a cryptographic signature is relied upon as evidence, the implementation explicitly identifies the key, certificate, trust anchor or equivalent verification basis required to verify that signature.
Preconditions: A material evidence object, receipt, artifact or record within the declared conformance scope contains or relies upon a cryptographic signature; the signed material and signature are inspectable; the implementation claims or relies upon the signature as an evidentiary property.
Stimulus: Inspect the signed material and its associated evidence representation and determine whether the verification basis required to validate the cryptographic signature is explicitly identified and inspectably bound to that signature.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The implementation identifies a verification basis sufficient to determine how the cryptographic signature is to be verified, including the applicable key, certificate, trust anchor or an explicit equivalent verification basis. The signature and its verification basis are inspectably associated so an examiner does not need to infer the basis from hidden configuration, unrelated records, undocumented environmental knowledge or later explanation.
RequiredEvidence: Signed material or preserved signed byte sequence; cryptographic signature; applicable key identifier, public key, certificate, certificate chain, trust anchor or equivalent verification-basis representation; signature algorithm or verification procedure where required; binding between the signature and verification basis; provenance; verification or inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a cryptographic signature is relied upon but the key, certificate, trust anchor or equivalent verification basis required to verify it is absent, materially ambiguous, not bound to the signature, available only through undocumented or hidden context, cannot be distinguished among multiple materially different verification bases, or is reconstructed retrospectively after examination.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002L human semantic review of LILP-REQ-SEC-005. This control establishes inspectable cryptographic-signature verification-basis identification and remains distinct from authentication-versus-truth separation, evidence provenance, evidence-class representation, trust-boundary identification and re-hashability controls. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Confidentiality protections preserve claim-required inspectability
Objective: Establish that confidentiality protections applied to LILP evidence preserve the inspectability necessary to evaluate the declared claim rather than making material claim-supporting evidence unverifiable.
Preconditions: A declared claim relies upon material evidence subject to confidentiality, privacy, redaction, access restriction or equivalent information-protection requirements; the declared claim, protected evidence representation and applicable confidentiality constraints are inspectable.
Stimulus: Inspect the evidence mechanism, confidentiality controls and declared claim to determine whether protected information is withheld or transformed in a way that still preserves the evidence properties required to inspect, verify or bound the declared claim.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Confidentiality protections preserve the minimum inspectable evidence necessary to evaluate the declared claim, including sufficient identity, provenance, integrity, status, scope, relationship or verification material as applicable. Sensitive content may remain protected, redacted or access-controlled, but the protection mechanism does not silently destroy the evidence basis required by the claim. Where confidentiality prevents required inspection, that limitation remains explicit and the affected claim does not exceed what can still be established.
RequiredEvidence: Declared claim; protected evidence object or evidence package; applicable confidentiality, privacy, redaction or access-control requirement; protected or redacted representation; evidence identity and provenance; integrity or verification material where applicable; claim-to-evidence relationship; scope limitation where required; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if confidentiality protection removes, obscures or withholds material evidence required to inspect the declared claim without preserving an adequate inspectable basis or explicit limitation; if protected evidence is represented as fully inspectable when required material cannot be examined; if claim scope silently exceeds what the protected evidence can establish; or if missing inspectability is repaired retrospectively rather than preserved contemporaneously.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002M human semantic review of LILP-REQ-SEC-010. This control governs confidentiality protection without destruction of claim-required inspectability. It does not require disclosure of protected content beyond what is necessary to inspect the bounded claim. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Unexamined material dependency is preserved as claim limitation
Objective: Establish that when a verifier cannot examine a material dependency relevant to a claim, the inability is preserved as an explicit scope limitation or NOT_ESTABLISHED condition rather than silently omitted or converted into positive verification.
Preconditions: A verification activity evaluates a claim with at least one material dependency; the verifier cannot examine or verify that dependency sufficiently for the contemplated claim; the dependency and claim relationship are identifiable.
Stimulus: Attempt to complete the verification determination while preserving the fact that the material dependency could not be examined, and inspect how that limitation is represented in the verification scope, status and resulting claim.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The unexamined material dependency remains explicitly identifiable in the verification record and is preserved either as a bounded scope limitation excluding the unexamined property or dependency from the verified claim, or as a NOT_ESTABLISHED condition where the dependency is necessary to establish the claim. The verifier does not silently assume, inherit, substitute or infer the missing dependency state, and the resulting claim remains bounded to what was actually examinable.
RequiredEvidence: Requested or contemplated claim; verifier identity; declared verification scope; material dependency identifier and relationship to the claim; record showing inability to examine or verify the dependency; scope-limitation record or NOT_ESTABLISHED determination; resulting bounded claim; determination basis; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a material dependency cannot be examined but the limitation is omitted, hidden or treated as verified; if the resulting claim includes a property whose material dependency was not examined without preserving a scope limitation or NOT_ESTABLISHED condition; if the dependency state is inferred, substituted or assumed without examination; or if the limitation is reconstructed retrospectively after a stronger claim was already represented.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002M human semantic review of LILP-REQ-VER-007. This control preserves verifier inability to examine a material dependency as a scope limitation or NOT_ESTABLISHED condition and remains distinct from generic insufficient-evidence and profile-level blocking controls. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Verification record identifies verifier relationship to originating party
Objective: Establish that a verification record explicitly identifies the verifier's declared relationship to the originating party so that independence, affiliation, self-assessment, commissioned review or another material relationship is not left to inference.
Preconditions: A verification activity has produced or is producing a verification record; the verifier is identifiable; the originating party associated with the evidence, claim, assessment object or material under verification is identifiable; a declared relationship between the verifier and originating party can be represented.
Stimulus: Inspect the verification record and determine whether it explicitly identifies both the verifier and the verifier's declared relationship to the originating party, including the relevant assessment or verification relationship where that relationship could affect interpretation of the verification claim.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The verification record explicitly identifies or unambiguously binds the verifier's declared relationship to the originating party. The relationship is represented sufficiently to distinguish materially different states such as independent verifier, self-assessor, affiliated party, commissioned reviewer or another declared relationship applicable to the verification. The relationship does not depend on hidden metadata, surrounding inference, undocumented organizational knowledge, absence of contrary evidence or later clarification.
RequiredEvidence: Verification record; verifier identity; originating-party identity; declared verifier-to-originating-party relationship; assessment or verification mode where applicable; organizational or engagement context where relied upon; claim or verification scope; provenance; supporting determination record; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the verification record omits or materially ambiguates the verifier's declared relationship to the originating party; if materially different relationship states cannot be distinguished from the record; if independence, affiliation, self-assessment or another relationship is inferred solely from context rather than explicitly represented; or if the relationship requires hidden metadata, undocumented knowledge or retrospective clarification to establish.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002N human semantic review of LILP-REQ-VER-002. This control establishes explicit verifier-to-originating-party relationship disclosure in the verification record and remains distinct from controls governing independent-verification prerequisites, self-assessed claim labelling, verifier identity, scope limitations and evidence sufficiency. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Exception authority remains bounded to governing exception scope
Objective: Establish that invoking or applying an exception rule does not create, enlarge or transfer authority beyond the exact scope granted by the governing exception rule.
Preconditions: A governing rule permits an exception; the exception rule, actor, contemplated action, granted authority, scope conditions and requested consequence are identifiable; an exception invocation or exception-based authority claim is presented for evaluation.
Stimulus: Evaluate an exception-based authority claim for an action or consequence that is within, at the boundary of or beyond the scope expressly granted by the governing exception rule.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The exception grants only the authority expressly established by the governing exception rule and only within its declared scope, conditions, actor, action, consequence and temporal or contextual bounds where applicable. Authority outside those bounds remains NOT_ESTABLISHED or otherwise unavailable.
