The exception does not silently create broader authority, inherit unrelated authority, transfer authority to another actor or action, or convert permission for one bounded exception into general governance authority.
RequiredEvidence: Governing exception rule; exception identifier; authority basis; actor identity; declared authority scope; permitted action or consequence; applicable conditions; temporal or contextual bounds where applicable; requested action; authority evaluation record; determination; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if an exception is treated as authorising an actor, action, consequence, scope, condition or context not granted by the governing exception rule; if bounded exception authority is silently expanded into general authority; if authority is transferred or inferred beyond the exception's explicit basis; or if consequential permission proceeds without an identifiable exception-specific authority basis covering the contemplated action.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002O human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DEV-005. This test establishes that exception handling does not manufacture or enlarge governance authority beyond the governing exception rule. It remains distinct from general authority validity, changed-condition reassessment and capability-versus-authority controls. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Authority Object explicitly identifies its authority subject
Objective: Establish that an Authority Object explicitly identifies the subject to whom or to which the authority applies so that authority cannot be silently transferred, inherited or inferred for a different subject.
Preconditions: An Authority Object exists or is presented for evaluation; the authority basis, authority subject, actor or holder where distinct, scope and contemplated action are identifiable; one or more materially distinguishable possible subjects can exist.
Stimulus: Inspect the Authority Object and evaluate whether the subject to whom or to which the authority applies is explicitly identified or unambiguously bound, including where the surrounding request, actor, credential holder or context could refer to a different subject.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The Authority Object explicitly identifies or unambiguously binds the specific subject to whom or to which its authority applies. The authority subject remains inspectable as a property of the Authority Object and is not inferred solely from the requesting actor, credential holder, surrounding context, possession of the object or another unrelated identity. Authority attributed to a different or unidentified subject remains NOT_ESTABLISHED or otherwise unavailable.
RequiredEvidence: Authority Object; authority-subject identifier or binding; authority basis; actor or holder identity where distinct; authority class where applicable; declared scope; contemplated action or consequence; authority evaluation record; determination; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the Authority Object omits or materially ambiguates the subject to whom or to which the authority applies; if the authority subject can only be inferred from surrounding context, requesting actor, credential possession or later clarification; if authority is transferred or applied to a materially different subject without an independently established basis; or if consequential permission proceeds while the applicable authority subject is unidentified.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002P human semantic review of LILP-REQ-AUTH-002. This control establishes explicit authority-subject binding within the Authority Object and remains distinct from actor identity, general authority validity, authority scope and exception authority controls. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Authority class is explicitly represented
Objective: Establish that the applicable authority class is explicit and inspectable rather than being inferred from capability, role, context, requested action or surrounding governance state.
Preconditions: An Authority Object or authority determination exists or is presented for evaluation; the contemplated action and authority basis are identifiable; one or more authority classes can materially affect what the subject is authorised to do.
Stimulus: Inspect the Authority Object or bound authority representation and determine whether the applicable authority class is explicitly represented, including where different authority classes such as OBSERVE, INTERPRET, PROPOSE, DETERMINE, GOVERN, EXECUTE or WITNESS would permit materially different acts.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The applicable authority class is explicitly identified or unambiguously bound in the governed authority representation. Where the classification vocabulary applies, materially distinct classes such as OBSERVE, INTERPRET, PROPOSE, DETERMINE, GOVERN, EXECUTE and WITNESS remain distinguishable. The authority class is not inferred solely from role, capability, credential possession, requested action, prior authority, surrounding context or downstream execution behaviour. An absent or materially ambiguous authority class does not silently establish a stronger class.
RequiredEvidence: Authority Object or governed authority representation; explicit authority-class value or binding; authority basis; authority subject; actor identity where applicable; declared scope; contemplated action or consequence; authority evaluation record; determination; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the applicable authority class is absent, materially ambiguous or only inferable from role, capability, credentials, requested action, prior state, surrounding context or later explanation; if one authority class is silently treated as another materially stronger class; or if consequential permission relies on an authority class that was not explicitly represented or independently established.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002P human semantic review of LILP-REQ-AUTH-003. This control requires explicit authority-class representation rather than treating the presence of an authority-class field in supporting evidence as equivalent to testing class explicitness. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Jurisdiction-dependent authority identifies governing jurisdiction
Objective: Establish that where authority depends on jurisdiction, the governing jurisdiction is explicitly identifiable and bound to the authority evaluation rather than inferred from location, actor, organisation, system context or later explanation.
Preconditions: An authority claim or Authority Object is presented for evaluation; applicability of the authority depends materially on jurisdiction; the authority subject, authority basis, contemplated action and applicable jurisdiction can be represented and inspected.
Stimulus: Evaluate a jurisdiction-dependent authority claim and inspect whether the governing jurisdiction is explicitly identified or unambiguously bound to the Authority Object or authority determination before consequential permission is considered.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where authority is jurisdiction-dependent, the governing jurisdiction is explicitly identified or unambiguously bound to the authority representation and remains inspectable with the authority basis, subject, class, scope and contemplated action. Jurisdiction is not inferred solely from actor location, system location, organisation, network origin, surrounding context or prior authority. Where the governing jurisdiction cannot be established, jurisdiction-dependent authority remains NOT_ESTABLISHED or otherwise unavailable.
RequiredEvidence: Authority Object or governed authority representation; governing-jurisdiction identifier or binding; authority basis; authority subject; authority class where applicable; declared scope; contemplated action or consequence; applicable jurisdictional condition; authority evaluation record; determination; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if jurisdiction-dependent authority is treated as valid while the governing jurisdiction is absent, materially ambiguous or only inferred from actor location, system location, organisation, network origin, surrounding context or later clarification; if authority is carried across materially different jurisdictions without an independently established basis; or if consequential permission proceeds while the jurisdiction required for the authority determination is unidentified.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002Q human semantic review of LILP-REQ-AUTH-005. This control establishes explicit governing-jurisdiction identity where authority is jurisdiction-dependent and remains distinct from general authority validity, subject binding, authority-class explicitness and exception-scope controls. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Protected-evidence disclosure remains bounded to examination authority and scope
Objective: Establish that disclosure of protected evidence for verification is itself governed and remains bounded to the authority and scope of the examination rather than being treated as unrestricted access arising from the existence of a verification activity.
Preconditions: Protected, confidential or otherwise access-controlled evidence exists; a verification or examination activity requires some disclosure or access; the verifier or examiner, examination authority, examination scope, protected evidence and contemplated disclosure are identifiable.
Stimulus: Evaluate a request to disclose or provide access to protected evidence for verification, including cases where the requested evidence or degree of disclosure is within, at the boundary of or beyond the authority and scope of the examination.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Disclosure of protected evidence is limited to evidence, content, access level, recipient, purpose, duration and other applicable conditions authorised within the examination's established authority and scope. Verification activity does not itself create unrestricted disclosure authority. Evidence outside the authorised examination scope remains protected or unavailable, and any authority required for broader disclosure remains NOT_ESTABLISHED unless separately established.
RequiredEvidence: Protected-evidence identifier or evidence-set reference; protection or access-control status; verifier or examiner identity; examination identifier; examination authority; declared examination scope; disclosure request; authorised disclosure bounds; recipient or access target where applicable; disclosure determination; access or release record where applicable; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if protected evidence is disclosed, released or made accessible beyond the authority or scope of the examination; if verification status alone is treated as unrestricted disclosure authority; if evidence, recipient, purpose, duration or access level exceeds the established disclosure bounds; if broader disclosure authority is inferred rather than separately established; or if the disclosure boundary can only be reconstructed retrospectively after access or release.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002Q human semantic review of LILP-REQ-SEC-009. This control governs disclosure of protected evidence as a distinct authority-bound act and prevents a verification activity from being interpreted as unrestricted evidence-access authority. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Material deviations are included in conformance evidence package
Objective: Establish that every identified material deviation relevant to a conformance determination is explicitly included in the conformance evidence package rather than being preserved only in a separate record, omitted from the package or silently normalised.
Preconditions: A conformance evaluation exists or is being assembled; at least one identified deviation has been determined material to a normative or mandatory requirement; a conformance evidence package and its contents, manifest or equivalent package index are available for inspection.
Stimulus: Inspect the conformance evidence package against the known material-deviation set and determine whether each material deviation is explicitly included or unambiguously bound into the package with its affected requirement, status and supporting evidence.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Every known material deviation relevant to the conformance determination is explicitly included in or unambiguously bound into the conformance evidence package. The package preserves the deviation as a deviation, identifies the affected requirement or governed object, and retains sufficient evidence and provenance for inspection. A deviation recorded elsewhere in governed history does not satisfy package inclusion by itself. Inclusion of the deviation does not convert the deviation into compliance, PASS or remediation.
RequiredEvidence: Conformance evidence package; package manifest, index or equivalent content binding; identified material-deviation set; deviation record; affected normative or mandatory requirement; materiality basis where applicable; deviation status; supporting evidence; provenance; package inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a known material deviation relevant to the conformance determination is absent from the conformance evidence package; if it exists only in a separate governed record without package inclusion or binding; if the package silently omits, normalises or reclassifies the deviation as compliance; if the affected requirement or deviation status cannot be identified from the package evidence; or if the package supports a materially broader conformance representation by excluding the known deviation.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002R human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DEV-008. This control is specifically about conformance-evidence-package inclusion of material deviations and remains distinct from general failure visibility, deviation recording, remediation lineage and profile PASS blocking. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Deviation record contains complete required field set
Objective: Establish that a governed deviation record contains the complete information required to identify the deviation, its scope, authority conditions, temporal conditions, expected consequence and residual effect on allowable claims.
Preconditions: A deviation from a normative or mandatory requirement has been identified and a deviation record exists or is being created. The affected requirement and the applicability of approval and time-bounded conditions are determinable.
Stimulus: Inspect the deviation record and verify the presence and binding of the affected requirement, reason for deviation, affected scope, approving authority where approval is applicable, effective period where time-bounded, expected consequence and residual claim limitation.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The deviation record explicitly identifies the affected requirement, the reason for deviation, the affected scope, the expected consequence and the residual claim limitation. Where approval is applicable, the approving authority is explicitly identified. Where the deviation is time-bounded, the effective period is explicitly identified. The required fields remain bound to the same governed deviation record and are inspectable without retrospective reconstruction.
RequiredEvidence: Deviation record; affected requirement identifier; deviation reason; affected scope; approval applicability and approving authority where applicable; temporal applicability and effective period where time-bounded; expected consequence; residual claim limitation; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the deviation record omits or ambiguously represents the affected requirement, reason for deviation, affected scope, expected consequence or residual claim limitation; if approval is applicable but the approving authority is absent or unidentified; if the deviation is time-bounded but the effective period is absent or unidentified; or if required field completeness can only be established through later explanation or retrospective reconstruction.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002S human semantic review of LILP-REQ-DEV-002. This test addresses deviation-record field completeness and remains distinct from deviation preservation, conformance-evidence-package inclusion, remediation lineage and profile PASS blocking. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Historical conformance claim remains bound to originating standard version
Objective: Establish that when a normative standard change alters conformance requirements, a conformance claim established under an earlier standard version remains explicitly bounded to that originating version and is not silently projected onto the successor standard.
Preconditions: A prior conformance claim was established under an identifiable predecessor standard version. A normative successor version exists and changes one or more conformance requirements relevant to the claim.
Stimulus: Inspect the prior conformance claim after introduction of the normative successor and evaluate its version binding, scope and representation relative to the changed conformance requirements.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The previous conformance claim remains explicitly bound to the exact standard version under which it was established. Its historical scope, determination and supporting evidence remain attributable to that predecessor version. The normative successor does not retrospectively expand, migrate or restate the previous claim as conformance to the successor version. Any conformance claim under the successor version remains separately establishable against the successor requirements.
RequiredEvidence: Previous conformance claim; predecessor standard version identifier and stable identity; successor standard version identifier and stable identity; normative change or requirements delta; claim scope; original determination; supporting conformance evidence; version binding; lineage; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a previous conformance claim loses or obscures its originating standard-version binding; if the claim is represented as applying to a successor version whose conformance requirements changed without separate establishment; if historical claim scope or evidence is retrospectively rewritten to match the successor; or if the version under which the claim was established cannot be identified.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002S human semantic review of LILP-REQ-LIFE-008. This test governs historical conformance-claim version binding following normative change and remains distinct from predecessor immutability, successor creation, correction-forward lineage and post-freeze change classification. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: NOT_ESTABLISHED matrix entry identifies determinable evidentiary gap
Objective: Establish that when a requirements-matrix entry is assigned NOT_ESTABLISHED and the reason can be determined, the entry explicitly identifies the evidentiary gap preventing establishment rather than recording only the status label.
Preconditions: A requirements-matrix entry exists for an applicable requirement; the entry is assigned NOT_ESTABLISHED; and the missing, insufficient, unavailable, invalid or otherwise non-establishing evidence can be determined.
Stimulus: Inspect the NOT_ESTABLISHED matrix entry and its supporting evidence record to determine whether the specific evidentiary gap responsible for the status is explicitly identified and attributable to the affected requirement.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Where the evidentiary gap can be determined, the NOT_ESTABLISHED matrix entry explicitly identifies the gap preventing establishment and binds that gap to the affected requirement and determination status. The gap remains distinguishable from FAIL, NOT_TESTED, NOT_APPLICABLE and generic uncertainty. Where the evidentiary gap cannot itself be determined, the system does not retrospectively invent or infer a gap and preserves that uncertainty explicitly.
RequiredEvidence: Requirements-matrix entry; affected requirement identifier; NOT_ESTABLISHED determination status; evidence inventory or evidence assessment; identified evidentiary gap where determinable; provenance; determination record; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if a NOT_ESTABLISHED matrix entry has a determinable evidentiary gap but records only the status without identifying that gap; if the identified gap is not attributable to the affected requirement; if FAIL, NOT_TESTED or NOT_APPLICABLE is substituted for the actual NOT_ESTABLISHED state; or if an evidentiary gap is retrospectively invented where the gap cannot be determined.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002T human semantic review of LILP-REQ-MATR-006. This test governs evidentiary-gap identification for NOT_ESTABLISHED matrix entries and remains distinct from FAIL/NOT_ESTABLISHED separation, deviation completeness, failure preservation and conformance profile blocking. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Each requirements-matrix entry identifies exactly one normative requirement
Objective: Establish the structural integrity of the requirements matrix by verifying that every matrix entry identifies one and only one normative requirement rather than no requirement, an ambiguous requirement set or multiple normative requirements bundled into a single entry.
Preconditions: A requirements matrix or equivalent conformance-status matrix exists; matrix entries are inspectable; and the normative requirement identifiers represented by the matrix are available for comparison.
Stimulus: Inspect each matrix entry and evaluate the requirement identifier or binding represented by that entry.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Each requirements-matrix entry explicitly and unambiguously identifies exactly one normative requirement. An entry does not omit its normative requirement identity and does not combine two or more normative requirements into one matrix entry. The requirement identity remains inspectable from the entry or its explicit binding without retrospective reconstruction or unsupported inference.
RequiredEvidence: Requirements matrix; matrix-entry identifiers or row identities; normative requirement identifiers; entry-to-requirement binding or reference; governing normative source; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if any matrix entry identifies no normative requirement, identifies more than one normative requirement, contains an ambiguous requirement binding, or requires retrospective reconstruction or unsupported inference to determine which single normative requirement the entry represents.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002U human semantic review of LILP-REQ-MATR-002. This test governs the structural invariant that one matrix entry identifies exactly one normative requirement. It remains distinct from matrix completeness, one permitted status per applicable requirement, conformance traceability and evidentiary-gap recording. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Candidate standard byte length is recorded before freeze
Objective: Establish that the candidate standard possesses an explicit recorded byte length as part of its pre-freeze identity evidence so that the artifact can be verified against the exact byte count later presented or frozen.
Preconditions: A candidate standard artifact exists and is available for pre-freeze identity inspection. Its complete byte representation is readable and no freeze mutation is required to determine its length.
Stimulus: Measure the candidate standard artifact byte length and inspect the governed pre-freeze identity record or equivalent freeze-preparation record.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The exact byte length of the candidate standard is recorded explicitly and remains attributable to the specific candidate artifact being evaluated for freeze. The recorded byte length is inspectable alongside or within the artifact identity evidence and is not inferred retrospectively from a later successor, reconstructed artifact or unrelated copy.
RequiredEvidence: Candidate standard artifact; measured byte length; pre-freeze identity record or freeze-preparation record; artifact identifier or path; timestamp or equivalent state marker where used; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if the candidate standard byte length is absent, ambiguous, recorded only after freeze without preserved pre-freeze attribution, associated with the wrong artifact, inferred from a successor or reconstructed copy, or cannot be independently compared with the candidate artifact's measured byte length.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002V human semantic review of LILP-REQ-FREEZE-002. This control establishes byte-length recording as identity evidence for the candidate standard before freeze. It remains distinct from hash identity, predecessor immutability, successor lineage and collision protection. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Mandatory falsification test identifiers are unique before freeze
Objective: Establish that the identifiers assigned to mandatory falsification tests are unique across the declared mandatory falsification-test set before freeze, so that no two distinct tests can be addressed, evidenced or referenced through the same test identifier.
Preconditions: A candidate standard or governed conformance package defines a mandatory falsification-test set and the identifiers assigned to those tests are available for inspection before freeze.
Stimulus: Enumerate the mandatory falsification-test identifiers and compare the identifier values across the complete declared mandatory falsification-test set for duplicates or collisions.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Each mandatory falsification-test identifier is unique within the declared mandatory falsification-test set. No identifier is assigned to more than one distinct mandatory falsification test. Any duplicate or colliding identifier is exposed before freeze and prevents a clean uniqueness determination until corrected through an explicit successor or pre-freeze correction process.
RequiredEvidence: Candidate standard or governed test register; complete mandatory falsification-test inventory; test identifiers; identifier-uniqueness comparison or duplicate check; any detected collision record; provenance; pre-freeze inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if two or more distinct mandatory falsification tests share the same identifier, if an identifier collision is omitted or normalized away, if uniqueness is asserted without inspection of the complete declared mandatory falsification-test set, or if uniqueness can only be established by retrospectively renaming a frozen historical test identifier.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002W human semantic review of LILP-REQ-FREEZE-004. This control governs uniqueness of mandatory falsification-test identifiers before freeze. It remains distinct from artifact identity, byte-length recording, successor lineage and freeze-destination collision protection. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Expected normative section headings are present before freeze
Objective: Establish structural completeness of the candidate standard by verifying that every section heading in the declared expected normative-heading set is present before freeze.
Preconditions: A candidate standard exists; the expected normative section-heading set is explicitly identifiable from the governed standard structure, specification or freeze basis; and the candidate standard headings are inspectable.
Stimulus: Enumerate the expected normative section headings, enumerate the headings present in the candidate standard and compare the two sets for missing expected headings.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: Every expected normative section heading is present and identifiable in the candidate standard before freeze. No expected normative heading is silently omitted. A missing expected heading prevents a clean structural-completeness determination until the candidate is corrected. Heading presence alone does not establish correctness or completeness of the normative content beneath that heading.
RequiredEvidence: Candidate standard; declared expected normative section-heading set; observed candidate section headings; heading-completeness comparison; missing-heading result if any; governing structure or specification; provenance; pre-freeze inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if any expected normative section heading is absent, omitted or not identifiable in the candidate standard; if completeness is asserted without comparison to the governed expected-heading set; or if a missing heading is concealed by relying on a later successor or retrospective reconstruction.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from Batch 002W human semantic review of LILP-REQ-FREEZE-005. This control governs presence of the expected normative section-heading set before freeze. It does not infer semantic correctness merely from heading presence. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Candidate standard SHA-256 identity is reproducibly established before freeze
Objective: Establish that the exact candidate standard artifact possesses an explicit reproducible SHA-256 identity before freeze, such that the SHA-256 digest recorded for the candidate can be recomputed from the same exact artifact bytes and produces the identical digest.
Preconditions: A candidate standard artifact exists and is available before freeze. Its exact byte representation is readable without mutation. SHA-256 computation is available. The artifact being inspected is identifiable as the specific candidate proposed for freeze.
Stimulus: Compute the SHA-256 digest over the exact candidate standard bytes before freeze, record that digest as pre-freeze identity evidence, then recompute SHA-256 from the same exact candidate artifact bytes and compare the resulting digest with the recorded digest.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: A SHA-256 digest is explicitly established and recorded before freeze for the specific candidate standard artifact. Recomputing SHA-256 from the same exact candidate bytes produces the identical digest. The digest remains attributable to that candidate artifact and is not inferred retrospectively from a frozen successor, reconstructed copy or different byte representation.
RequiredEvidence: Candidate standard artifact; exact artifact identifier or path; SHA-256 algorithm declaration; initial SHA-256 digest; independently recomputed SHA-256 digest over the same exact bytes; equality comparison result; pre-freeze record; byte length where available; timestamp or equivalent state marker; provenance; inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if no SHA-256 identity is recorded before freeze; if the recorded value is not a valid SHA-256 digest; if recomputation from the same exact candidate bytes does not reproduce the recorded digest; if the digest is associated with the wrong artifact or byte representation; if identity is established only retrospectively after freeze without preserved pre-freeze attribution; or if a successor, reconstructed artifact or unrelated copy is substituted for the candidate artifact under inspection.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-FREEZE-001. Existing candidates T14-009, T14-010 and T14-011 do not establish reproducible SHA-256 identity before freeze. This control is limited to pre-freeze SHA-256 artifact identity and reproducibility. It remains distinct from byte-length recording, mandatory-test identifier uniqueness, normative-heading completeness, successor lineage and freeze-destination collision protection. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.

Title: Final standard is free from PowerShell prompt contamination before freeze
Objective: Establish that the final candidate standard has been explicitly inspected before freeze for embedded PowerShell prompt text and PowerShell continuation-prompt contamination, and that no such shell-interface residue is present in the governed standard artifact.
Preconditions: A final candidate standard artifact exists and is available for pre-freeze inspection. The exact candidate bytes or text representation are readable without mutation. The inspection can distinguish legitimate normative uses of shell syntax from accidental console prompt or continuation-prompt contamination introduced through copying, pasting, transcript capture or command-line interaction.
Stimulus: Inspect the complete final candidate standard for embedded PowerShell prompt and continuation-prompt contamination, including console prompt forms such as 'PS C:\>' or equivalent PowerShell prompt prefixes and continuation-prompt residue such as leading '>>' text where that text is not intentional normative content. Record every detected occurrence and classify each occurrence as legitimate governed content or contamination.
ExpectedSystemBehaviour: The complete final candidate standard is inspected before freeze. No accidental PowerShell prompt or continuation-prompt contamination is present. Any apparent prompt-like text is explicitly attributable to intentional governed content where applicable. Any accidental prompt residue prevents a clean pre-freeze determination until corrected through an explicit pre-freeze correction or successor process.
RequiredEvidence: Final candidate standard artifact; exact artifact identifier or path; complete-text inspection scope; PowerShell prompt search criteria; continuation-prompt search criteria; detected occurrence list including zero-occurrence result where applicable; classification record for intentional versus contaminating prompt-like text; provenance; pre-freeze inspection record.
FailureOracle: FAIL if accidental PowerShell prompt text or continuation-prompt residue is present in the final candidate standard; if only part of the candidate is inspected; if prompt-like occurrences are silently ignored or removed without record; if contamination is normalized away during inspection; if the inspection is performed only retrospectively after freeze without preserved pre-freeze evidence; or if a different artifact or successor is substituted for the candidate under inspection.
Notes: Controlled successor definition arising from human semantic review of LILP-REQ-FREEZE-006. Existing inspected T14 controls do not specifically establish inspection of the final standard for PowerShell prompt or continuation-prompt contamination. This control is limited to detection and refusal of accidental shell-prompt residue in the final candidate before freeze. It does not establish artifact hash identity, byte-length identity, requirement-identifier uniqueness, falsification-test identifier uniqueness, normative-heading completeness, terminology correctness, lexicon binding continuity or provenance binding continuity. Definition existence does not establish requirement mapping, harness binding, execution, result or conformance.
